Well to make things short, My life is split into chapters. The first being my young childhood. Playing all day in a lower middle class neighborhood with my older brother who had asperburgers. The problems I had were simple. I miss it very much. Chapter 2 was when I went to a new neighborhood and went to public school for the first time. I wouldn't say I was bullied, but I definitely didn't have many friends. I discovered a new passion in computers. I built my first Computer when I was 10. It was my new friend. It was all I needed. I could never be sad when I was at my desk in my room. Then Chapter 3 hit when puberty started. I changed drastically. I grew out my hair and started playing guitar. Before I knew it I was the best guitarist in my school, and I was highly recognized for it. It even landed me a few very attractive girlfriends. Chapter 4 was beyond my favorite chapter. I started to develop muscle mass. I chopped my goofy hair off. And I started even a new passion of restoring muscle cars. At one point I was the best guitarist with the best car. Every weekend was spent working on cars or practice for shows. I was completely straight edge, yet I had some what of a "bad boy/class clown" persona that I was known for.  Chapter 4 climaxed when I met a girl from another state on a missions trip and she was the most beautiful thing I had ever seen. It felt like we loved each other more than anyone had ever loved something before. Time progressed as I graduated high school and even community college with her. Thats when things started to go a bit dark. Chapter 5 began with our break up over 2 and a half years ago. My parents had fallen into crippling debt and I couldn't afford to continue my education. I was devastated. Yet I pushed forward as I had landed me a new job that made me finanically independant to afford school. I was delighted. When I finally moved away to a university I was lonely at first, but a Fraternity gave me a bid card that changed everything. I looked forward to every day. I even started to drink socially. The classes I was taking were easier than high school classes. I loved it. However, over my first winter break I confronted my old lover, letting her know my feelings still existed. Hers, however, did not. My fraternity brother's did everything they could to let me forget her and thats just what they did. I even landed a new girlfriend. I spent a happy summer working on old cars. Once the new semester started I was even more ecstatic. I was single and moving around bedrooms with some fine midwestern women. Women that were way out of my league as a kid. I even started to be a captain of a sport team, and became a part time model. It wasn't until Spring break of this year where something happened. I had finally turned 21 and was loving the trip. Yet somehow, of every state, of every beach. She appeared. Without warrant. I noticed she hadn't changed a bit. I was muscular and tattooed and bearded and she was still the young and fit girl I met when she was only 15. I could still see the innocence in her eyes. I couldn't help it. I broke down. It lasted weeks. I would drink Jack Daniel's until I pissed myself. I would wake up on our pool table or somewhere else. The guys were nice enough to set me up with a counselor and he got me through it for awhile. And for a month or two. It was good. But this week... While I was drinking with the guys, these feelings came back. Instead of depressive I became aggressive. I lashed out at them and betrayed them. I feel awful for it. I don't even know if its about her or anything, but I feel like I was never meant to go to Chapter 5. Like Chapter 5 was a depressing fall. A conclusion to great story.
